column1: # Champion|Hypothetical decision and its reasoning; editorial extension of notes.tsv

Aatrox|Your first swing misses its useful edge and the opponent backs toward reinforcements. Do not spend every remaining movement option trying to repair that opening. Move sideways with your frontline, threaten the escape route with chains and rebuild a clean swing angle. Judge the next cast by where the opponent can move, not by the original target location.

Ahri|Charm misses and the enemy carry retreats behind a teammate. Keep the remaining Spirit Rush movement for a new angle or retreat rather than crossing both opponents. If an ally then holds a reachable target, use that setup for the orb sequence. A failed first catch can become safe pressure; it need not become a failed dive.

Akali|Shuriken Flip marks a retreating target, but their support moves beside the landing point. Delay or give up the follow rather than treating the mark as a commitment. Use shroud to change the next angle while allies advance. Re-enter when the support spends the response that would otherwise stop your damage and exit.

Akshan|A Scoundrel is low behind a wall while another enemy stands along your swing route. First damage the target you can reach from allied protection. The revival incentive does not remove collision risk or enemy follow-up. Take the swing only when its path and endpoint improve your position even if the first target survives.

Alistar|An enemy carry is in Headbutt range, but a diver is already beside your marksman. Turn toward the diver and choose a displacement that creates room for your ally. An offensive combo would remove your protection from the important fight. Once the carry can move and attack again, reassess whether a forward engage is still useful.

Ambessa|Two enemies line up for Public Execution, with the farther one standing beyond your team's approach. Change the line or keep the ultimate available. Selecting the nearer-looking threat is not enough if the spell will carry you deeper. When you do arrive, preserve the attack-and-cast rhythm so the follow-up does not exhaust your resources.

Amumu|Bandage Toss connects while your teammates are clearing a wave behind you. Do not assume a connected skillshot creates immediate damage support. Use the control window to return toward them unless they can join safely. When allies are in range, place the next control sequence where their damage can cover the held targets.

Anivia|Your storm covers the river entrance, but an ally is retreating through the same narrow space. Place the wall only after checking which side each teammate will occupy. Splitting two enemies is useful; cutting off your own carry may undo that value. Hold the stun for the enemy who crosses the zone toward you.

Annie|You have a stun ready and see two enemies near Tibbers range. One ally is still too far away to damage them, and a diver is approaching your carry. Keep the stun threat between that diver and your team. A smaller defensive catch can create a much cleaner follow-up than a larger unsupported burst.

Aphelios|You approach an objective expecting a familiar weapon combination, then notice ammunition is nearly spent. Check which pair will actually be available when contact begins. Adjust your position before the swap rather than discovering the changed pattern during a dive. Use Moonlight Vigil for the equipped weapon's job, with protection appropriate to the range you intend to hold.

Ashe|An enemy retreats slowly while their assassin is missing. Continue attacking only while your route stays beside allied protection. Keep the arrow for the assassin if that is the threat preventing safe damage. Hawkshot can help check the next approach; a slowed opponent is still able to lead you toward an unseen teammate.

AurelionSol|Singularity controls an entrance, but an enemy moves around the side toward your channel position. Break the damage sequence and reposition behind allies. Keeping the breath active is less valuable than preserving another safe spell cycle. Use flight only after checking the route for the control that could interrupt your escape.

Aurora|Between Worlds creates a useful fighting area and an opponent moves toward its edge. Do not assume the opponent must remain inside. Use your next movement to keep a safe landing and a useful curse-return line. If allies cannot cover the far side, maintain pressure from your current edge rather than hopping after the retreat.

Azir|An enemy carry is visible beyond the frontline and a shuffle looks possible. Your own carry is already being threatened. Keep soldiers on the reachable fight and use Emperor's Divide to deny the diver's access. Your sustained attacks can decide the exchange without a deep entry that removes the team's protected damage source.

Bard|Two opponents cluster for Tempered Fate just as an ally begins a committed damage sequence. Delay the stasis or aim at the enemies outside that sequence. Freezing the intended victims could deny your own team's timing. Prepare the next binding angle and a portal route before the stasis ends so the pause becomes an advantage.

Belveth|A takedown leaves coral beyond the enemy frontline. Keep attacking the reachable opponent until the route opens. Collecting the reward is a separate decision from earning it. Use the available dash directions to preserve contact and an exit; do not stand still in enemy control because Royal Maelstrom is ready.

Blitzcrank|A hook can hit either an exposed damage dealer or the tank standing beside them. Adjust the angle for the useful target, or hold the threat. Pulling the tank may place their engage beside your carry. If they enter anyway, use the knock-up and silence to protect your team rather than helping their approach.

Brand|Several enemies cluster, but a diver is crossing toward you. Build a usable stun sequence on that immediate threat before spending all spells on the cluster. Once allies screen the approach, spread damage and choose a bounce path through the remaining group. Total possible damage matters less than surviving long enough to apply it.

Braum|Your shield faces the main ranged threat while a second opponent approaches from the side. Move with your carry and turn attention toward the new angle. Mark the closer threat for allied stun follow-up. The original shield direction is a choice to update, not a safe position that remains valid through the whole fight.

Briar|Blood Frenzy begins pulling you toward a target under hostile protection. Use the planned Chilling Scream exit before the pursuit becomes unrecoverable. Your team can keep pressure while you regain control. Review whether the target's retreat was predictable at activation; the best correction may be a later entry rather than a faster cancel.

Caitlyn|An ally controls an opponent just beyond the frontline. Place a useful trap follow-up while remaining behind protection. Do not walk through a second enemy merely to force the next attack. Keep the net for the approaching threat and let the prepared traps shape where the opponent can safely retreat.

Camille|You can isolate the enemy carry, but your team is occupied by their frontline. Wait until allied damage has a route to the target or use your pressure to help the nearer fight. Hextech Ultimatum restricts the victim's movement; it does not prevent their teammates from helping or make an unsupported duel favorable.

Cassiopeia|Your poison misses as a target begins moving away. Re-establish the setup instead of spending repeated Twin Fangs into an unfavorable sequence. Miasma can restrict the route when its placement is safe. If the enemy turns toward your team, reconsider the ultimate angle while preserving enough space to keep casting after the first exchange.

Chogath|A mobile opponent steps into Rupture range, then pauses with an escape available. Aim at the route they must use or wait for allied setup. Stay between the immediate threat and your damage dealers. Save Feast for a reachable finish rather than abandoning that position to pursue the same opponent through their teammates.

Corki|Missiles reach an opponent behind their frontline, but your next attack would require a forward Valkyrie. Keep the dash unless the landing is safe against the remaining threats. Continue ranged pressure and move around the edge with allies. A spell hit does not require an immediate attack follow-up when the ranges create different risks.

Darius|You have built pressure on a frontline target while their carry remains distant. Continue the useful close exchange instead of abandoning it for a long chase. Place the outer Decimate edge carefully and watch allied support. Consider the ultimate when the finish is plausible; do not assume the reward can rescue an unsupported approach.

Diana|Several enemies are close enough for Moonfall, but your teammates have no clear route to them. Hold the entry or choose the nearer edge of the formation. Once allied damage is ready, use the prepared dash sequence and pull to hold enemies where follow-up lands. A large hit count alone does not justify becoming surrounded.

DrMundo|A cleaver hits a retreating carry while your allies are still fighting their frontline. Occupy the useful route instead of running out of support range. Time recovery around the pressure you expect to absorb. Your presence can create safe allied damage even when you cannot force the distant target to stand and fight.

Draven|An axe falls toward an enemy's ready control spell. Give up the catch and keep a safe attack position. Use Stand Aside if it can interrupt the approach, then rebuild your attack rhythm from protected ground. In review, separate the lost axe from the larger benefit of avoiding a disable that would stop every subsequent attack.

Ekko|Parallel Convergence threatens the choke, but your Chronobreak return point is now close to an enemy flank. Do not use the old return location as an assumed escape. Wait for a better sequence or take a shorter trade beside allies. Check both your entry and return positions before turning the delayed zone into a commitment.

Elise|Cocoon misses and the opponent steps behind allied protection. Stay in a position where another catch is possible rather than switching to spider form solely to continue the attempt. When a target is controlled, close with a clear purpose and retain a useful Rappel option. Plan the landing after the avoidance, not just the dodge itself.

Evelynn|Allure threatens an exposed opponent, but nearby enemies begin moving toward your approach. Change the angle instead of revealing into prepared protection. When allies occupy that response, commit to the vulnerable target with an ultimate exit directed away from the dangerous formation. A hidden approach has value only while the destination remains useful.

Ezreal|Your shots repeatedly hit the frontline while the carry stays behind it. Keep attacking a safe target and move to improve the firing line. Do not spend Arcane Shift forward just to create one clear shot. Save it for the engage that changes your position; consistent mixed attack and spell damage can outperform an unsafe carry chase.

Fiddlesticks|Your planned Crowstorm channel spot becomes visible before the contest. Move to a new angle or use defensive control while allies hold space. Repeating the exposed entry gives enemies time to interrupt or leave. When a hidden approach is available, confirm that teammates can reach the landing before committing to the channel.

Fiora|Grand Challenge exposes a vital on the far side of a target surrounded by teammates. Take the accessible contact and preserve Riposte for the meaningful response. Do not run through the group just to complete the pattern. If a crowded fight prevents useful movement, consider whether safe side pressure would have created a better decision before grouping.

Fizz|A vulnerable target is close, but enemy control is still waiting for your landing. Hold the evasive tool or delay the entry until that response is occupied. A useful ultimate hit can let allies prepare the fight first. Choose the landing route as carefully as the damage sequence so a surviving target does not strand you.

Galio|An ally is being attacked in river and offers a Hero's Entrance destination. Check whether they can remain in useful ground and whether other teammates can join. If the landing would isolate you both, support the retreat by another route. On a good arrival, control the immediate threat before pursuing a distant opponent.

Gangplank|You prepare a barrel chain at an objective, but an enemy can freely contest its first barrel. Move the protected anchor or wait until an ally pressures that opponent. Use Cannon Barrage to shape the route the enemy needs rather than relying on an easily removed chain. Preserve enough setup for the next approach if the first attempt fails.

Garen|The enemy carry retreats beyond your approach while their diver reaches your teammate. Turn the silence and close pressure onto that diver. Use Courage for the retaliation you can see coming, then look for a realistic ultimate finish. You do not need to reach the original carry for the fight to use your champion's strengths.

Gnar|Your rage is not ready for the planned wall-side engage. Communicate the changed timing and use ranged pressure without wasting the escape. If the transformation arrives while allies are retreating, hold useful ground instead of forcing the old plan. The available form and team position must agree before a good wall angle becomes a good entry.

Gragas|A barrel ultimate could knock an enemy toward your team or scatter them away from allied damage. Decide the desired destination before casting. If your carry is under threat, displacement away from them may matter more than a catch. Leave room to follow the new target position rather than aiming only at where the enemy stands now.

Graves|A nearby target is reachable, but units and terrain restrict your firing line. Move to a cleaner angle with your team before spending movement aggressively. Use smoke to interfere with the relevant enemy's view while keeping a route back. Close pressure is useful only if your attacks actually reach the intended target and the return exchange is survivable.

Gwen|You can begin attacking the frontline while the enemy carry remains outside easy reach. Use that contact and place the mist for the threats it can actually exclude. Watch enemies entering the protected area rather than treating it as total safety. Keep movement available to adjust the damage line when the opponent changes direction.

Hecarim|A fast flank reaches the enemy backline before your team can cross the river. Slow the commitment or choose a nearer line that allies can follow. Use disruption to create a shared damage window, then remain connected to your team. Arrival speed is useful when it changes a coordinated fight, not when it merely makes you the first isolated target.

Heimerdinger|The fight begins outside your prepared turret area. Fall back through that setup if your team can use it, or prepare new ground before committing. Do not chase a low target until your damage sources stop covering the exchange. Choose the empowered spell for the immediate control or pressure need rather than following one fixed sequence.

Hwei|An ally needs protection while an enemy is also available for poke. Choose the spell family that solves the urgent problem before returning to damage. Keep distance while selecting the next control shape. The useful question is which cast lets your team continue the fight, not which sequence uses the greatest number of different spells.

Illaoi|A spirit is available near your tentacle setup, but the opponent starts retreating into open ground. Hold the area where your pressure is prepared. Let the spirit and tentacle threat discourage their return rather than chasing away from your support. Commit the ultimate when enemy contact is sustained, not merely because one target briefly enters reach.

Irelia|A marked target offers a dash deeper into the enemy team, but it removes the route back through nearby units. Keep the safer sequence and attack the reachable opponent. Use the next mark or allied control to reassess access. Fast movement through targets is a resource to plan, not a reason to consume every available dash.

Ivern|An ally approaches the target of your root while another ally is about to take damage. Support the teammate who can use the next shield, and direct Daisy toward the immediate threat. Do not follow the rooted target simply because access is offered. Your position should preserve support range for the part of the fight that remains winnable.

Janna|A diver reaches your carry while other opponents retreat. Use your control and movement support to remove that immediate access. If Monsoon is needed, consider where its displacement sends enemies and whether the channel location remains safe. Chasing with your last defensive tool can turn a protected carry into the next easy target.

JarvanIV|Cataclysm can hold a carry, but an allied ranged damage dealer would be left outside a safe firing position. Check follow-up and escape paths before creating the arena. Against a diver, the same control may protect your backline instead. Terrain that catches an enemy can also constrain allies; judge the resulting formation rather than the initial hit.

Jax|Counter Strike is ready while the enemy's key response is still available. Use a measured approach and reserve a useful leap target for leaving. If the opponent retreats beyond allied support, stop the pursuit and protect the next attack window. A strong duel pattern loses value when several enemies can control your landing in sequence.

Jayce|Your ranged pressure lowers an opponent's health, but they remain beside two allies. Continue from a safe firing angle instead of automatically switching to a melee finish. Enter close range only when the return exchange and exit are manageable. Treat each form change as a new range decision rather than the next required step of a combo.

Jhin|The fourth shot is ready as an enemy moves toward cover. Check the approach before following, and use allied damage to create a safer Deadly Flourish opportunity. During reload, reposition instead of lingering at the same exposed angle. Start Curtain Call only when the team can protect the channel from the missing threat.

Jinx|A low-health enemy could trigger your passive, but reaching them requires passing your frontline. Damage the nearer safe target and let allied pressure create the first takedown. When the reset arrives, check the next threat before moving forward. Keep traps for the route an enemy must cross to stop your continued attacks.

KSante|All Out could remove a threatening opponent, but your carry would then be alone against a second diver. Stay in the protective role until that second threat is controlled or another ally can cover it. Isolation is a change of responsibility. Evaluate the team position left behind, as well as the duel you expect to take.

Kaisa|An ally marks a carry on the far side of the fight. Compare the available landing sides before using Killer Instinct. If none offer support or a safe next move, keep damaging the reachable frontline. A mark creates an option; it does not require abandoning the position from which your current damage is already helping.

Kalista|Your oathsworn ally is threatened while you are building spears on a reachable enemy. Choose whether Fate's Call is a rescue or an engage before using it. Keep a clear hop route while that decision resolves. Do not move into a wall or crowded corner just to maintain attacks on the original spear target.

Karma|A tether is close to completing, but maintaining it would pull you away from an ally under pressure. Preserve the team's position with shielding and movement support instead of chasing the tether at any cost. Choose Mantra for the current problem. The strongest continuation may be a safe retreat followed by another supported exchange.

Karthus|You can pressure the contested area from behind allies, but stepping forward would expose you to an avoidable death. Keep the living position and another spell cycle. If you do die, use the passive window on the actual fight rather than automatically choosing the ultimate. Decide whether a channel contributes more than immediate local pressure.

Kassadin|Several Riftwalk casts have brought a carry into reach, but your remaining mana may not cover the return. End the chase and rebuild resources before re-entering. Wait for an allied damage window that reduces the distance you must cross. The relevant resource check includes the exit cast, not only the next cast that reaches the enemy.

Katarina|A dagger gives access to a damaged group while one enemy still holds an interrupt. Wait until that response is used or attack a safer edge with allied help. After the first takedown, reassess each reset landing. A new available cast does not remove the danger at its destination or guarantee the next channel can continue.

Kayle|Your ultimate is available while a teammate takes nonlethal poke before the main fight. Preserve it if they can safely retreat. During commitment, protect the ally whose survival allows the team to keep dealing damage, including yourself when focused. Use the temporary window to improve position so the team is not still trapped when it ends.

Kayn|Your team groups at an entrance and you are deciding how to approach. With Rhaast, look for sustained contact beside allied pressure; with Shadow Assassin, seek a vulnerable edge and a short exit sequence. Do not carry a plan from one form into the other. Terrain access still needs a useful destination and a response plan.

Kennen|The enemy can see your direct route toward their clustered team. Change the flank or wait for allied pressure to occupy their disengage. Once you enter, stay close to the targets your allies can damage. A possible multi-target ultimate is less valuable when opponents can simply move away before your team reaches them.

Khazix|A separated carry moves close to their support as you approach. Reassess the isolation opportunity before using Leap. Wait for another separation or help finish a target already damaged by allies. Use invisibility to change the timing of the attempt, and keep an escape option if the enemy's formation stays too compact.

Kindred|Both an ally and an enemy are low inside the area where you could cast Lamb's Respite. Decide who can act when the zone ends before committing it. Keep your team in a position to control that final exchange. Preventing the first death is only part of the decision when the same protection also preserves the opponent.

Kled|Your charge reaches a target and Skaarl leaves during the response. Reassess the available movement and health instead of continuing the mounted plan. Take a realistic remount opportunity only when contact is survivable. If allies cannot follow, a retreat can be better than betting the whole fight on recovering the mount before the next enemy sequence.

KogMaw|Bio-Arcane Barrage is ready, but no enemy is safely in range. Wait for the frontline to establish contact rather than spending the window during approach. Once attacking, keep a protected route behind you. Use the downtime to reposition; stretching for one extra attack can expose a champion with no dash to the next engage.

Leblanc|Distortion gives a useful angle on a carry, but an enemy moves toward the return pad. Treat both locations as threatened. Use a shorter sequence or change the next approach rather than returning automatically. If backline access closes, a chain on a diver can help the team more than repeated attempts into a watched entry point.

LeeSin|Sonic Wave hits a target beyond your allies. Check the landing and the intended kick direction before following. If a useful Dragon's Rage would still leave you isolated, keep the second cast unused. A defensive kick on the diver already near your carry may create more value and preserve a reliable route back through allied units.

Leona|Solar Flare catches an enemy just as your team begins retreating. Do not follow with Zenith Blade unless their movement changes and damage support is real. Use the catch to secure space for the retreat. When allies are ready, layer the next control rather than spending every disable at the same instant without additional benefit.

Lillia|Dream Dust is active on two useful targets while a third stands deep inside the enemy team. Take the coordinated sleep opportunity already available. Chasing the third mark may expose you to control before your team can act. Signal the timing and prepare follow-up so the sleep becomes shared damage rather than several disconnected attacks.

Lissandra|Your claw reaches a deep position, but the enemy turns toward its endpoint. Keep the recast unused or choose a less committed approach. If you enter, decide whether the ultimate must control an enemy or preserve your own survival. Self-stasis buys time only when allies can make that time useful and the exit position remains supportable.

Locke|Ritual Nails creates a mark on a target near allied pressure, but your health is already low. Consider Soul Ignition's cost before starting the continuation. Take reachable attacks while staying connected to teammates, and preserve Purgatory for a realistic finish. Delayed recovery is not immediate protection against the burst that can arrive during entry.

Lucian|An opponent is within dash range while their engage remains ready. Keep the dash for the response and weave attacks after safe spells from your current angle. If close contact is too dangerous, use The Culling from a supported line. Judge an offensive dash by the position after the burst, not just the damage it starts.

Lulu|Your carry wants help chasing while an assassin is missing from view. Keep polymorph available for that access threat and avoid spending every tool offensively. When the assassin appears, protect the carry's ability to move and attack. Use Wild Growth where the health and nearby disruption change the immediate exchange rather than as a late reaction to a lost position.

Lux|Light Binding connects, but reaching a passive attack would put you inside the enemy frontline. Follow with safe spell damage and keep your distance. Send the shield through the allies who will take the response. The caught target is already useful setup; it does not require sacrificing the range advantage that protects your next spell cycle.

Malphite|A three-target ultimate is available behind a wall while only one ally can follow. Compare it with stopping the enemy already threatening your carry. A smaller engage with immediate damage support can be more decisive. Check where you will stand after the impact, because reaching the targets does not provide a dependable way back out.

Malzahar|A priority enemy enters ultimate range while a second opponent has a clear path to interrupt you. Move behind protection or wait for that opponent to be occupied. Use the suppression when allies can both damage the target and protect your channel. The target selection and your own standing position must be good at the same time.

Maokai|Nature's Grasp can cross an open area, but opponents have room to step away. Shape the approach toward a route they need or combine it with allied pressure. Use saplings to check useful brush before advancing. If divers reach your carry first, turn the close control into protection rather than chasing the original initiation plan.

MasterYi|Two damaged enemies are visible, but several hard disables remain ready. Let allied pressure draw out the relevant control before entering. Use Alpha Strike for a meaningful response or follow, then reassess the next landing. The first reset is a possible reward for a good entry, not evidence that an unsupported opening will work.

Mel|An enemy approaches with a threat that is not answered by projectile destruction. Keep distance and use Solar Snare or allied protection instead of relying on Rebuttal for universal safety. Build marks through reachable contact, then judge whether Golden Eclipse contributes to a useful finish. Spend the defensive response on the exchange it can actually change.

Milio|Your carry can attack safely if the diver is kept away, while a distant enemy offers easy poke. Preserve the kick for that diver and keep support range on the carry. Use the campfire where attacks can continue. Shield and cleanse during relevant pressure rather than letting the team walk forward merely because all support tools are ready.

MissFortune|Several enemies line up for Bullet Time, but the missing diver has an unchecked path to your channel location. Move behind protection or wait for their access to be occupied. Once the firing spot is safe, use allied control or terrain to hold the line. Canceling an unsafe channel can preserve a later contribution.

Mordekaiser|You can take a low enemy into Death Realm while your team is about to finish them safely. Consider removing a different threat instead, or keep the ultimate. Ask what the remaining fight becomes without you and the selected opponent. Also check the return position; a won duel can still end with you surrounded when the isolation ends.

Morgana|Black Shield is ready as harmless pressure lands before an enemy's key disable. Save it for the action that would stop your ally from fighting or escaping. If binding misses, give ground instead of walking forward to force Soul Shackles. The ultimate needs a survivable proximity window, not simply a group of targets nearby.

Naafiri|A wounded target offers a pursuit into their grouped team. Wait for allied pressure to make the landing useful, and reserve The Call of the Pack for the response that matters. After the first sequence, reassess any second pursuit. A low target and available recast do not guarantee that the next destination is safe.

Nami|An opponent approaches through Tidal Wave's path while your ally is ready to attack. Layer the bubble on the more predictable movement instead of rushing an unsupported cast. Heal and empower the ally who can maintain contact afterward. Keep enough space to continue support rather than walking into danger to improve one bubble angle.

Nasus|A carry is too far away to hit, but Wither can restrict the threat pressuring your team. Use the slow for that shared fight and attack a reachable opponent. Do not abandon allies to chase the ideal damage target. Large stacking potential only becomes useful when you can actually maintain contact through the enemy response.

Nautilus|Your hook would reach the enemy frontline, but its landing draws you away from a diver near your marksman. Turn the close control onto the diver instead. If the team regains position, select a Depth Charge target that creates useful follow-up. Count both where the hook goes and where it leaves the allies you were protecting.

Neeko|A disguise offers an approach toward several enemies, but your allies are not close enough to use the control. Hold the uncertainty and improve their route before revealing. Once the team is ready, choose a landing that keeps the important targets within follow-up. Surprise helps start the sequence; it does not supply the damage after it.

Nidalee|A spear hits a target near their protected frontline. Do not automatically jump into cougar range. Compare the landing with the enemy responses still available and continue ranged pressure if the close sequence is unsafe. Use the hit to improve space with allies; a successful setup can be valuable even when you decline the immediate follow.

Nilah|Allied protection is ready, but the opponent still has room to disengage from your approach. Keep a movement option for the continuation instead of spending every dash to arrive. Enter when allies can sustain the close fight and use the ultimate where their damage can follow. Recheck the formation if enemies leave your effective range.

Nocturne|Paranoia reveals a reachable carry standing beside several teammates. Darkness does not remove their protection. Choose a more supportable target or wait for separation while allied pressure begins. If you enter, prepare the spell shield for the response that would stop your contact and maintain the tether only while the landing remains survivable.

Nunu|A snowball route reaches the enemy, but a ready interrupt can stop Absolute Zero immediately. Use the entry for layered control and wait for a better channel opportunity. Cover or allied disables can make the later cast more useful. Decide which allies can follow before committing to a long approach that ends beyond their damage range.

Olaf|Ragnarok is available, but the target keeps moving beyond your team's support. Do not confuse resistance to control with protection from damage or loss of contact. Take the reachable fight and retrieve axes only along survivable routes. The useful commitment is one where repeated attacks can continue, not merely one where enemies cannot disable you.

Orianna|Your frontline moves forward with the ball while an enemy diver turns toward your body. Verify the ball's actual position before using Shockwave, then decide whether to keep the offensive setup or support the retreat. Your casting position and the ball's influence are separate. A strong placement is not enough if you are forced out before the sequence.

Ornn|The ultimate's return line is useful, but an enemy can interrupt you at the recast position. Improve your standing ground or wait for allied control before beginning. After the knock-up, use terrain-based follow-up only where the geometry works. A clear first line should not distract you from the space and timing required for the second action.

Pantheon|The targeted stun reaches an enemy while another threat moves behind you. Choose the Aegis Assault facing for the important incoming damage, then reposition as the threats split. Check the Mortal Will state before the sequence so the empowered action serves the plan. Directional defense does not make standing between opponents safe.

Poppy|An enemy prepares a dash toward your carry while a tempting wall stun is available elsewhere. Keep Steadfast Presence near the carry and stop the important access first. Use the wall angle only if it preserves that protection. A charge that pushes a target away from allied damage may reduce the value of the team's existing setup.

Pyke|An enemy reaches a possible execution window but still has movement or a save available. Wait for that response to be occupied, or use the hook and stun to help allies secure the target. Do not turn the indicator into a promise. Check the ultimate's landing and the next escape route before attempting the finish.

Qiyana|The enemy moves from wall-side ground into an open area as you approach. Reassess the element and ultimate plan before committing the familiar sequence. Use concealment or a different angle to maintain options. A combo prepared for one terrain layout may no longer create useful control or leave the same safe exit.

Quinn|Fast travel brings you to a fight before your teammates finish approaching. Enter from a supported edge rather than becoming the first visible target. Use blind on a relevant threat and judge Vault by its landing position. Speed helps choose when to arrive; it does not make an unchecked arrival into several enemies survivable.

Rakan|You can reach a useful group, but your nearest ally is moving away from the Battle Dance return route. Wait until the route exists again or take a shorter entry. After the disruption, return toward support instead of extending the chase. An engage plan includes the allied position after your first move, not only before it.

Rammus|Your approach meets a tank while the enemy's attack threat stays farther back. Decide whether taunting the tank helps the current fight or merely lets the important opponent attack freely. If a diver reaches your carry, interception may be the better target. Use the defensive stance around real contact and stay where allies can exploit the control.

RekSai|Burrowed information suggests a target near a wall, but other enemies remain unseen. Use the signal to guide a checked approach, not to declare the target isolated. Plan the tunnel and allied follow-up before the knock-up. Take the ultimate finish only if the destination remains safe after the opponent's teammates respond.

Rell|A distant cluster offers a large crash-and-ultimate opportunity while your carry is retreating from a diver. Turn the control toward the fight your allies can actually use. If you later engage forward, choose a place where the group can remain in allied damage. A committed entry is difficult to rescue when teammates cannot cross the gap.

Renata|An ally is about to take lethal pressure but has no reachable target for a takedown. Do not assume Bailout guarantees their recovery. Use displacement, shielding and a useful Hostile Takeover line to improve the situation first. When Bailout is appropriate, the ally needs a realistic action during its window, not merely permission to keep advancing.

Renekton|A side entry is available, but fury is unprepared and both dashes would be needed just to arrive. Use a shorter exchange or wait for a better setup. If your carry is threatened, an empowered stun on the diver may be the useful role. Preserve a route back after the initial pressure rather than planning only the burst.

Rengar|An ultimate approach exposes a carry beside ready protection. Do not jump just because the target is available. Wait for the response to be used and choose the empowered ability for the actual need: damage, control or recovery. After landing, a surviving target requires a fresh decision rather than an automatic extended trade inside their team.

Riven|Reaching the target would consume all movement and leave no defensive action for retaliation. Take a shorter sequence beside allied pressure and preserve one answer to the response. When the target becomes finishable, choose a useful ultimate line before it escapes. Mechanical speed improves an appropriate sequence; it cannot replace a supportable entry position.

Rumble|The enemy approaches a narrow route while your Heat is close to changing what you can cast next. Prepare the spell sequence before drawing The Equalizer along their movement path. Stay beside the burning area with allied pressure. An impressive ultimate line has little value if enemies can leave and your next intended spell is unavailable.

Ryze|A reachable opponent threatens your carry while a distant target offers more attractive damage. Use the prepared root on the immediate threat and keep casting from a safe distance. Reserve Realm Warp for a destination the team has checked. Moving together is useful only if the arrival offers a better fight or a real escape.

Samira|Allied control creates an entry, but Style is not ready and an enemy interrupt remains unused. Build a safe sequence before committing to Inferno Trigger. Use Blade Whirl for a meaningful projectile exchange rather than assuming it answers every disable. After a reset, inspect the next landing before carrying the same momentum deeper into the formation.

Sejuani|The ultimate catches an opponent beyond your team's current damage range. Use the space it creates to move together rather than charging alone. Once allies are close, layer frost and other control on the reachable threat. If their melee pressure is elsewhere, adjust your expected follow-up instead of assuming the full planned sequence will occur.

Senna|Mist appears on the enemy side of a dangerous control line. Give up the pickup and keep a position that supports safe attacks and useful healing lines. Use the root on the approach that threatens the formation. Evaluate the ultimate across the active fight, including allied shielding, rather than only looking for a distant finishing shot.

Seraphine|A long Encore line appears through allies and enemies, but reaching it would require leaving protection. Let allied movement improve the corridor or choose a shorter useful line. Plan the echoed spell for what follows the control: survival may matter more than extra poke. Keep the next cast available from a position where delayed spells can still connect.

Sett|An enemy tank is available for the ultimate while your team has already placed damage elsewhere. Choose a landing that supports the shared fight instead of carrying the tank away from it. As damage builds Grit, aim Haymaker where opponents must move and use its shield before lethal pressure. Waiting for maximum value can become waiting too long.

Shaco|Your clone pressures one route while the real body is near a possible area-damage response. Keep the body safe and use prepared boxes to constrain pursuit. Do not treat enemy attention on the clone as proof that nearby damage cannot reach you. If the target stays protected, reset the approach rather than forcing a prolonged exposed trade.

Shen|An ally needs Stand United while an enemy is close enough to threaten your channel. Move to a safe casting position and assess whether the ally can survive until arrival. On landing, taunt the immediate threat and place the defensive zone where teammates can use it. The rescue includes both the channel and the fight you enter afterward.

Shyvana|Dragon Form creates an entry into the enemy approach, but allied damage is still behind you. Use the transformation along a supportable route and bring the shield window into meaningful contact. If opponents disengage, return toward the team instead of extending the chase. Judge the active form and current kit rather than relying on an old single-spell play pattern.

Singed|An opponent follows your poison trail while the main fight moves away. Return toward space your team can use instead of continuing a separate chase loop. Use adhesive and fling to place a reachable threat into allied damage or away from your carry. The opponent taking damage matters only if your movement also supports the actual contest.

Sion|An open approach offers a long ultimate, but allies cannot follow the full distance. End the entry where the team can join and layer the charged control on an occupied target. Do not demand a full unprotected charge into ready interrupts. If killed, pressure a reachable opponent with the passive rather than assuming it repairs the original positioning error.

Sivir|Your team wants to cross an exposed route while enemies hold several engage tools. Use On the Hunt for a coordinated entry or retreat, then preserve Spell Shield for the most important response. Blocking one spell does not justify moving past protection. Keep attacks on the safe target and let the formation support continued ricochet pressure.

Skarner|A wall route creates an approach, but dragging the captured targets forward would remove them from allied damage. Choose the Impale destination before committing. Keep the movement within support range and use the wall geometry deliberately. A successful suppression should improve the formation your teammates can use, not simply relocate opponents as far as possible.

Smolder|A stack opportunity requires flying forward beyond your frontline. Keep the safe farming or damage position and reserve movement for enemy access. During the fight, cast and attack the targets protection makes reachable, then aim the ultimate through the active contest. Development comes from continued participation; a dangerous extra stack can end several future opportunities.

Sona|An empowered attack is available, but using it would place you ahead of the ally you are supporting. Keep cycling support from protected range and choose the effect for the next safe exchange. Use Crescendo when it stops an important dive or extends allied control. Surviving for another aura cycle can matter more than forcing the current attack.

Soraka|A distant ally requests healing while an assassin threatens your route toward them. Maintain your own safe position and heal the ally who can still use the support. Place Equinox on the critical approach or cast and consider Wish before the useful save window ends. Losing the healer beside an isolated teammate can remove support from the entire fight.

Swain|The ultimate is active, but opponents move out of useful drain range while your team retreats. Do not chase alone through their ranged damage. Use control to maintain a reachable fight or leave with allies and prepare the next contact. Sustained healing and damage require sustained access; activation alone does not guarantee that access will remain.

Sylas|You have stolen a strong engage ultimate while your carry is under attack. Decide whether using it offensively would abandon the more important fight. The borrowed spell may instead provide protection, or you may need your own control first. Use passive attacks and Kingslayer in a reachable exchange rather than letting the stolen spell dictate an unsupported entry.

Syndra|A sphere line could poke several enemies, but spending the push leaves no response to a nearby diver. Hold the displacement until that access is answered or an ally can cover it. Burst the reachable target after useful control, then reposition during cooldowns. Keeping one defensive cast can preserve the next entire damage sequence.

TahmKench|An offensive opportunity opens while your carry is within reach of an enemy diver. Keep Devour available for the ally unless another teammate can reliably protect them. After the rescue, choose a safe position for the continuation. Moving away for personal pressure can remove the very tool the team's formation depends on.

Taliyah|Unraveled Earth covers an entrance and a target steps near its edge. Choose the Seismic Shove direction that moves them through the prepared area without disrupting allied positioning. Use Weaver's Wall only after checking friendly routes too. Terrain control is valuable when it improves both the enemy's constrained path and your team's ability to follow or retreat.

Talon|Your intended escape wall has already been used, but an exposed carry is still available. Find another exit before starting the burst or delay the attempt. Approach while allied pressure divides attention, complete the useful sequence, then leave. A wall on the map is not automatically an available escape in the current pursuit.

Taric|An enemy commits toward your linked ally and lethal damage is about to follow. Start Cosmic Radiance with its delay in mind and use the stun to disrupt the wait. Keep both relevant positions useful rather than wandering away during preparation. The cast must arrive while allies are alive and able to act, not after the danger has already resolved.

Teemo|A prepared mushroom route covers one approach, but the enemy chooses a clear path around it. Reposition with allies rather than chasing them outside the setup. Use blind on the relevant attacker and keep distance from spell threats it does not answer. Traps influence movement; they do not guarantee that opponents will walk through the planned damage.

Thresh|Death Sentence lands while your ally needs a lantern route out. Stay at the safe anchor instead of automatically taking the recast. Use Flay or The Box to disrupt pursuit and let the hook create time. A successful catch creates several options; joining the target is only one of them and may remove the best rescue position.

Tristana|Explosive Charge is on a low target, but jumping forward would depend on a takedown reset that has not happened yet. Keep attacking safely until the finish is realistic and the landing is clear. Use Buster Shot to remove a diver if needed. A possible reset should not be the only route out of your planned entry.

Trundle|Pillar can stop a retreating enemy, but its placement would also block your carry's route away from a diver. Choose the terrain position for the more important movement. Use Subjugate on a suitable durable target and continue reachable attacks. Sustained contact helps only while the team's formation remains able to support the exchange.

Tryndamere|Undying Rage is active and the target keeps moving away through enemy control. Use the remaining window to leave rather than spending all of it on pursuit. Plan the spin route before the protection ends. Surviving the current damage does not remove disables or ensure that the next position is survivable once the window closes.

TwistedFate|Destiny reveals a carry with a seemingly open landing behind them. Check nearby enemies and the ally who can follow before traveling. A safer edge arrival with a prepared Gold Card may offer the better catch. After landing, your movement options are limited, so information should change the destination rather than merely confirm that a target exists.

Twitch|Camouflage offers a firing line through several enemies, but the position is isolated from your support. Shift toward a safer edge before revealing. Once Spray and Pray begins, watch when enemy attention turns toward you and move with protection. A lined-up opening does not justify remaining in place through the response that ends your attack window.

Udyr|Your awakening is available before a small exchange near the objective. Decide whether spending it now leaves the wrong tool for the real commitment. During entry, choose the stance for contact, survival or disruption rather than cycling without purpose. If no target remains reachable, return to allied space instead of chasing solely because a movement tool is active.

Urgot|Circling a target would expose you to several enemies while some shotgun-leg angles remain unused. Take the safe angles and preserve contact beside your team. Use Disdain for a useful collision, then consider the ultimate on a realistic finish. Completing every directional damage opportunity is less important than staying alive for the next controlled exchange.

Varus|You are charging a shot while an enemy gains direct access to your position. Stop prioritizing the distant target and use movement, control or allied protection to answer the approach. Decide whether the current fight supports spell pressure or repeated attacks. Chain of Corruption can defend the formation as well as begin a forward catch.

Vayne|Two attacks have landed on a frontline opponent, but completing Silver Bolts would require tumbling into ready control. Keep the safe angle and wait for the next reachable contact. Save Condemn for the diver or a real wall opportunity. Finishing one passive cycle is not worth losing the position that permits every later cycle.

Veigar|Event Horizon surrounds an enemy who is already close enough to threaten you. Move away and use allied protection rather than assuming the cage makes its interior safe. Place delayed damage on the restricted route and burst a reachable target. The perimeter controls movement; opponents inside it still have actions you must respect.

Velkoz|A clear beam line appears while a missing enemy could reach your side. Keep the knock-up for that approach and improve your channel position before using the ultimate. Land repeated setup from protection instead of chasing an ideal angle. A slightly shorter safe damage window can be more useful than a full channel attempted from exposed ground.

Vex|Shadow Surge hits a carry inside a protected group while your fear is needed against a diver. Keep the recast unused and stop the immediate entry first. When protection is occupied, reconsider a follow-up landing with allies. The ultimate hit gives access, but the fear state and the enemy's remaining responses determine whether that access is useful.

Vi|Your ultimate can reach the carry beyond several teammates, but allied damage cannot follow the travel. Hold it or use the same reliable access on the diver threatening your backline. A guaranteed arrival does not guarantee a winning fight. Check the landing position, nearby enemies and your team's route before selecting the target.

Viego|A low-health opponent offers a possible possession, but you would have to start the fight alone to reach them. Help allies secure a reachable first takedown instead. After possession, quickly check the body's location and usable tools before extending. Each reset creates another decision; it does not erase the risks that remain around the new position.

Viktor|Gravity Field covers the route of an approaching diver, but they can reach you before the delayed control resolves. Reposition immediately and keep allied protection between you. Steer the storm with the active fight while preparing another cast cycle. A zone that will become dangerous later is not a substitute for space you need right now.

Vladimir|You can reach several enemies with Hemoplague, but pool would leave you in the middle of their waiting team. Delay entry until allied pressure occupies the response. Track health spent on the sequence and the next useful recovery window. Avoid using the whole evasive period without improving the position where you will reappear.

Volibear|Your marked target retreats beyond allies while another enemy threatens the nearby fight. Reassess the stronger follow-up bite rather than chasing it automatically. Place Sky Splitter where the shield and contact overlap, then pressure what your team can reach. Keeping a mark is valuable only while the target's position supports a survivable continuation.

Warwick|A low-health trail leads toward several unseen enemies. Treat it as a reason to check the route, not an instruction to leap. Use the defensive howl before the important incoming burst when you do commit. A suppression on the diver near your carry may offer more reliable value than pursuing the distant wounded opponent.

MonkeyKing|Your clone creates uncertainty, but allied follow-up is still outside the fight. Wait or take a short exchange instead of committing Cyclone alone. Once teammates can act, disrupt the reachable group and reposition between actions. The clone can complicate the enemy's response; it does not prevent area damage or make a known real-body location safe.

Xayah|Several feathers are behind the enemy frontline, but the diver approaching you is outside their return lines. Move backward to improve the geometry before using Bladecaller. Use Featherstorm for a meaningful incoming response and plan the new feather pattern. Count useful crossings through the relevant target rather than merely counting feathers on the ground.

Xerath|Your ultimate can finish a distant opponent while nearby vision is incomplete. Check the flank and whether allies can protect your standing position before channeling. Keep the stun for the enemy who could interrupt the attempt. If access changes, give up a shot and move; long range is useful only while the casting location remains safe.

XinZhao|Crescent Guard separates you from distant damage, but an opponent moves inside its boundary. Continue treating that close enemy as a real threat. Keep contact with a reachable target while staying beside allied follow-up. Do not stand still because the ultimate is active; the defensive boundary changes which threats matter rather than removing all of them.

Yasuo|An ally knocks up a target deep in the enemy formation while your safe dash units are behind you. Check the ultimate landing before following. It may be better to damage the frontline and use Wind Wall for the important projectile exchange. An airborne target is an available option, not proof that your team can support the arrival.

Yone|Soul Unbound begins from exposed ground and an enemy moves toward your body. Reassess the spirit-form chase before the return forces a bad position. Use the prepared Q or ultimate on a useful line only if the return remains manageable. Review the original body placement; many later escape problems began before the first forward move.

Yorick|Your team starts grouping while graves, walkers and Maiden are not prepared for immediate pressure. Decide whether catching safe side resources or arriving for defensive control is more useful than a late forced entry. When grouped, mark an accessible target and protect the summons' contribution. Do not walk Maiden through the frontline simply to appear active in the fight.

Yunara|The team is ready to fight, but Transcendence is unavailable. Plan spacing around the movement tools you actually have instead of assuming the upgraded dash exists. When the empowered state is ready, activate it for sustained reachable contact. Use the ranged slow through the approach while keeping allied protection close enough to support continued attacks.

Yuumi|Your attached ally dives beyond support while a safer teammate remains nearby. Consider transfer safety before moving; detaching into enemy control may make the situation worse. Shield during meaningful pressure and aim Final Chapter through useful lines. Attachment follows the host's positioning, so the decision includes which ally can realistically use your support without taking a doomed route.

Zaahen|A close fight starts before the required passive state is ready. Build Determination through reachable contact instead of assuming the revive already protects an aggressive entry. Use movement and pull to maintain a supportable exchange, then place Grim Deliverance where its damage and healing affect the fight. Recheck the state before taking a risk that depends on it.

Zac|Elastic Slingshot can land on several distant enemies while allies remain blocked by terrain. Choose a nearer landing or wait for their approach. After entry, collect blobs along safe routes and use disruption to keep useful targets in allied reach. Recovery and revival tools do not make an isolated landing into enemy-controlled ground a sound opening.

Zed|Death Mark reaches a carry while an enemy moves toward your visible shadow. Track both the current target and the return locations before spending another swap. Land the needed follow-up from a supportable angle, then leave before the enemy covers the exit. The mark is not a guaranteed finish when the damage sequence cannot safely connect.

Zeri|Burst Fire is blocked by an opponent while the desired target retreats toward terrain. Move to a clearer line with allied protection rather than using Spark Surge into unseen ground. Keep contact during the ultimate window only while the next position remains safe. Momentum is useful when shots connect and the enemy cannot freely close onto your route.

Ziggs|A distant target offers more bomb damage while a diver threatens your side. Keep Satchel Charge for displacement or your own escape, and place mines on the relevant approach. Use the ultimate where allies constrain movement. Spending the satchel for minor poke can remove the tool that would preserve several later safe casts.

Zilean|Chronoshift can save a teammate who is surrounded, but allies are already leaving the area. Consider where that teammate will revive and use movement or control to improve the follow-up. Apply the ultimate before lethal damage when the save is meaningful. Preventing the first death is not a complete rescue if the revival position remains uncontested enemy ground.

Zoe|Portal Jump creates a long Paddle Star angle, but an enemy is moving toward your known return point. Keep the original position protected before taking the cast. Use sleep setup from a safer line or delay the attempt. The portal extends your action range; it does not provide a lasting escape from a diver waiting for your return.

Zyra|Your plants cover an entrance while a wounded enemy moves out of that area. Hold the prepared ground and keep the root for the next approach. Use the ultimate across the useful plant zone rather than chasing into open space. If opponents remove the setup, rebuild with allies before assuming the same route is still controlled.
